title: Democracy
summary: System of government where supreme political authority is vested in the people, pioneered as direct democracy in classical Athens under Cleisthenes and Pericles.

title: Rule of Law
summary: Principle that all members of a society, including lawmakers and rulers, are equally subject to publicly disclosed, independently adjudicated legal codes.

title: Republic
summary: Form of government in which the country is considered a 'public affair' (res publica) and offices of state are held by election rather than hereditary right.

title: Socratic Method
summary: Form of cooperative argumentative dialogue between individuals, based on asking and answering questions to stimulate critical thinking and expose underlying contradictions.

title: Theory of Forms (Platonism)
summary: Philosophical doctrine holding that non-physical, eternal, and immutable Forms or Ideas represent the most accurate reality, of which material objects are imperfect reflections.

title: Formal Logic
summary: The systematic study of valid inference, argumentation, and syllogistic reasoning established by Aristotle in the Organon, underpinning scientific deduction for millennia.

title: Stoicism
summary: Hellenistic philosophy founded by Zeno of Citium and practiced by Seneca and Marcus Aurelius, teaching that virtue is the only true good and happiness comes from rational self-mastery.

title: Roman Jurisprudence
summary: The legal system developed across a millennium from the Twelve Tables to Justinian's Corpus Juris Civilis, forming the foundational core of modern continental civil law.

title: Citizenship
summary: Status of a person recognized under the custom or law of a sovereign state, granting specific civic privileges, voting rights, and legal protections in exchange for civic duties.

title: Ma'at (Cosmic Truth & Order)
summary: Ancient Egyptian ethical and cosmic concept of universal truth, balance, cosmic order, harmony, law, morality, and justice personified as a goddess.

title: Cuneiform Script
summary: One of the earliest systems of writing, invented by Sumerians in ancient Mesopotamia, using reeds to make wedge-shaped impressions on clay tablets.

title: Scientific Method
summary: Empirical method of acquiring knowledge characterized by careful observation, rigorous skepticism, hypothesis formulation, experimental testing, and measurement.

title: Monotheism
summary: The belief in the existence of one unified deity, early iterations seen in Akhenaten's Atenism and fully realized in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

title: Confucianism
summary: Ancient Chinese ethical and philosophical system developed from the teachings of Confucius, focusing on filial piety, moral righteousness (Ren), and ritual propriety (Li).

title: Buddhism
summary: Spiritual tradition founded on the teachings of Gautama Buddha, centered on understanding the nature of suffering (Dukkha) and achieving liberation through the Eightfold Path.

title: Human Rights
summary: Moral principles or norms that set out certain standards of human behavior and are regularly protected in municipal and international law as inalienable fundamental rights.

title: Constitutionalism
summary: The political philosophy holding that governmental authority is derived from and limited by a fundamental body of constitutional law.

title: Capitalism
summary: Economic system based on the private ownership of the means of production, market competition, and their operation for profit.

title: Theory of Evolution
summary: Biological principle stating that the diverse species of living things develop and adapt over generations through natural selection and descent with modification.

title: Artificial Intelligence
summary: The simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems, enabling reasoning, knowledge representation, problem solving, and adaptive learning.
